publication_endpoint: independent comparative test of life-history-state by landscape-opportunity control of realised mobility
core_hypothesis: realised mobility is a gated phenotype produced by internal movement state x landscape opportunity x local refuge value
primary_predictions: movement increases sharply when individuals transition from yellow/growth state to silver/migratory state
landscape permeability and hydrological opportunity modify the magnitude or timing of that mobility release
local refuge stability suppresses yellow-stage exploration more strongly than it suppresses silver-stage migration
stage-specific landscape effects outperform a single movement rule across systems

falsification: stage effects disappear after body size/season/tracking-design control
landscape opportunity does not interact with state
same environmental effects apply unchanged across yellow and silver stages
